title: Priority, Assignment & Delegation
origin: Preserved from the RN Quest v0.1 Lesson 1 pilot
html:
Management of care asks the RN to coordinate safe care while keeping accountability visible. The recurring exam question is not simply who can perform a task, but which client needs RN judgment now.

Start with acuity and change

  • Unexpected change, instability, or an immediate threat outranks routine scheduled care.
  • Use airway, breathing, circulation, acute neurologic change, and safety risk as rapid priority screens.
  • Compare the client with their own baseline. A new finding may matter more than a chronic abnormal value.
Shift rule
See the unstable or newly changed client first. Stable, predictable needs can usually wait long enough to address an immediate threat.

Delegate the task, not the judgment

The RN keeps initial assessment, interpretation, care planning, teaching, and evaluation. A trained assistive team member may perform a routine task for a stable client when the task is within role, directions are clear, and the RN follows up. Scope and facility rules always control.

Close the loop

A safe handoff names the current problem, recent change, action taken, response, and next concern. When delegating, state what to do, what finding to report immediately, and when the RN will reassess.
